That all men are created equal, that we have this incredible human dignity that is beyond. Any worth imaginable, each and every one of us at each and every stage. background.speaker: [target]
background.text: You know, what it was about, I'm opposed to abortion. I think this is killing of a innocent, a purely innocent human life. background.text: I think that, and this year, by the way, one of the projects we're doing at Priests for Life is going to focus even more on late-term abortion because, you know, that law that you signed and so many other efforts within the pro-life movement have been based on a simple conviction that to educate and move the public on abortion, we've got to start with what's most obvious. Obviously, it's a baby from fertilization, but it's more obvious to them that these babies are, in fact, one of us. They should be protected. And then when we start talking about the science about how they feel pain, it's even more persuasive to the public that these babies should be protected. So we're going to keep pushing on this. And I think we have, and I like your comments on this in terms of strategy going forward, I know that we've got the public opinion with us when it comes to late-term abortion. And I know that many members of Congress currently, would be of the same mind. And of course, even, you know, President Trump has spoken a lot about late-term abortion. We're not saying when we focus on late-term abortion, we're not saying that the earlier abortions are okay. We're just trying to lead people from where they are to where we need to go. What is your thinking on that?

ground_truth: I think we have to do it. We've got to convince the public that this is wrong. And the best and the easiest way to do it is is on these things like like late term abortions when it's so obvious this is a child. And in many in some cases, this child could survive outside of the womb. So, you know, we just can't do it. The other thing I think we need to do is I think we really need to start going at these. Some of these categories of abortions that just that we we we way over the number of percentages get aborted, like Down syndrome children, a Down syndrome child treated with decent care can live to retirement age and are now yet 90 plus percent of them get aborted in the womb. I ask people, how many Down syndrome children have you seen recently? And they're just they're not here. We kill them. They're killed in the womb. And I think we should start setting numerical targets like we want to reduce the number of Down syndrome abortions by 50 percent over five years and do it by state or community that we want to do that in the state of Kansas. Reduce these by 50 percent. And if people say, look, I'm all for you. I can't handle a special needs child. I'm not capable of it. Great. We've got to. I think we really need to start targeting in on some of those categories and numerically say this is what we're going to do with big press conferences, do it state of Texas, state of New York, other states that this is going to be our target. And people may react initially going. Yeah, well, wait a minute. And we've got to assure people we've got folks that will adopt them because we do. But I think we need to move forward in those categories as well.

ground_truth: Ambassador-at-Large covers the world, so I would travel all over the world in that position. I was promoting religious freedom. And that's why you're seeing so many authoritarian governments, particularly like China, Russia, North Korea, Cuba, really go at religious leaders, because those are the people who are going to be the leaders of the world. Those are the ones that can actually threaten their regime. And so they view religious freedom as an existential threat to their future. And we look at it as a fundamental human right, complete different worldviews that we have on that right.

background.speaker: SPEAKER_04
background.text: President Trump did so much in his administration the first time. He's already done so much in the second term. And I remember, for example, orders that he was issuing in terms of even training people from the United States who work internationally to be attuned to signs of religious persecution. And so that if they're trained to be sensitive to that, they can take steps or notify the administration in appropriate ways of what's going on in some of these other countries that they serve in. And it's so basic. I mean, it's a constitutional right in our own constitution precisely because, like you just said, it's a human right, the human right given to us by God to seek him, to believe in him. To hold to that belief as we see it, and then to profess it and live according to it. All of this is part of religious freedom. I think a lot of people feel like, or they might have just this basic notion that, oh, well, it's the right to be of whatever religion you want and to worship in church on Sunday or any other day that you want to go. Okay, that obviously includes that. But isn't a lot of the battle also in the arena of, okay, if I'm of a particular religion and my religion teaches me that certain things are wrong, then I'm going to be of a particular religion. And if I'm of a particular religion and things are right or wrong, I have to be able to live accordingly in the way I conduct my business, in how I educate my children, even in what I do in terms of my leisure activities, how I'm able to travel, how I'm able to spend money. In other words, religious freedom really is freedom in every aspect of life, isn't it?

ground_truth: It really is. And look how much enriched we've been as a country because we've honored this. We have Orthodox Jews that practice a different way. And yet you're kind of going, great, God bless you that you want to do that. We've got Amish. We've got a number of Amish in the state of Kansas that drive horse and buggy down our highways on the shoulders. And we've always found a way in the past to accommodate people of deeply held religious convictions because it's a very religious, spiritual country. And we prosper based upon people really bringing their passions and living them out in the public square. You know, what you're seeing in so many countries is this is getting thwarted. It's people getting killed. In Congo, you had 70 Christians slaughtered last week, 10 days ago. So by a militant Islamic group. And that's not an unusual thing, unfortunately, anymore for Christians to get slaughtered in different places, particularly in that contested area of Africa. But, yeah, it's the right to practice your faith. What you see in the West is this effort to suffocate religious freedom. Like we, I helped form a group national committee for religious freedom. And we got debanked within two months of forming the organization. The large multinational bank said, yeah, we're closing your account down. You'll see people get de-platformed, de-insurance, debanked. I saw a crisis pregnancy center get de-insurance. They just said, well, we're not going to give you.
